title: High-Value London Property Near Buckingham Palace Attached By ED In Rs 1,400 Crore Bank Fraud Probe
text:
News Brief
Swarajya Staff
Jan 01, 2026 | Updated 10:51 AM GMT+5:30

The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has provisionally attached a London property valued at Rs 150 crore near Buckingham Palace in connection with an alleged bank loan fraud and money laundering case involving textile firm S Kumars Nationwide Ltd and its former CMD Nitin Kasliwal.
In a statement, the federal investigation agency stated on Wednesday (31 December) that a provisional order was issued under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) on Tuesday to attach the asset.
According to the agency, the “high-value” property valued at Rs 150 crore near the Buckingham Palace is held under the “beneficial ownership” of Nitin Shambhukumar Kasliwal and his family members.
Kasliwal is accused of defrauding a consortium of Indian banks to the tune of Rs 1,400 crore, the agency said.
The ED said that after attaching overseas assets, it coordinates with counterpart agencies in the concerned country to take possession of such properties under criminal provisions of the anti-money laundering law.
The agency alleged that Kasliwal, through S Kumars Nationwide Ltd, cheated banks and “diverted” funds outside India in the guise of foreign investments, later acquiring immovable assets overseas that were “concealed” through complex networks of private trusts and companies in foreign jurisdictions.
The ED carried out searches in the case on 23 December, during which documents and devices were seized.
According to the agency, a detailed analysis of the said material revealed that Nitin Kasliwal established a complex network of trusts and companies in multiple offshore tax havens, including the British Virgin Islands, Jersey, and Switzerland
“The investigation found that Nitin Kasliwal set up the Catherine Trust (formerly Surya Trust) in which he and his family members were the primary beneficiaries,” the agency said.
The agency said the trust “controlled” a Jersey and British Virgin Islands-based company, Catherine Property Holding Limited, which ultimately owned the London immovable property that has now been attached.
